bullets.title: NVDA/AI infrastructure: Jensen + Trump reject AI slowdown; semis testing trend but demand intact
bullets.body: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang publicly rejected Anthropic's call to slow AI development at the All-In Summit, joined by Trump in a live call; both argued slowing down would cede ground to China. Mizuho and MS note AVGO revenue targets unchanged, active managers holding AI longs awaiting valuation reset, and order visibility extends through 2027. Hedgeye remains the key bear, calling the semi complex an 'imploding bubble' with NVDA testing trend breakdown and maintaining 0% semi exposure.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity surge: CRWD +14%, PANW +13% on AI-safety rotation; software vs semis largest spread ever
bullets.body: Software outperformed semis by +11.3% on 9/14 — the first time the spread closed above +10% since 2006 — as AI-safety concerns drove rotation into cybersecurity. CRWD is up 101% YTD with 1M realized vol at 1-year highs (87.7); PANW up 13% in a single session. JPM and Citi both flag cybersecurity as 'non-discretionary' in the AI era, with machine-speed threats requiring autonomous defense across CRWD, PANW, ZS, OKTA.

bullets.title: META: Launches Meta One subscription tiers ($2.99–$499/mo); Arke chip deploy H1 2027; Hedgeye flips bullish
bullets.body: Meta launched Meta One globally with individual plans (WhatsApp Plus $2.99, Instagram Plus $3.99, bundles to $19.99) and creator/business tiers up to $499/mo, covering AI features, verified badges, and Meta Business Agent. Separately, Bloomberg reports Meta will deploy its in-house Arke chip in H1 2027, with next-gen Astrid by end-2027. Hedgeye flipped META from bearish to bullish, calling it 'the biggest bullish breakout among mega-caps.'

bullets.title: MU: World's first 512GB DDR5 module demoed; DRAM supply tightening into 2027, price hikes expected
bullets.body: Micron demonstrated the world's first 512GB DDR5 RDIMM on multiple server platforms, with volume production targeted for H2 2027. MS TMT notes DRAM module makers expect supply to tighten further in 3Q26 (especially DDR5), with 2027 supply allocation potentially halved vs. 2026 and sequential price increases expected — debate is whether single-digit or double-digit. Hedgeye has MU as an official short.

bullets.title: AMD: Pre-quiet period call bullish; targeting 50%+ CPU server share on Venice/2nm ramp
bullets.body: Wolfe Research and Piper both flag AMD's pre-quiet period call as 'reassuring' — CPU and GPU ramps on track with demand running ahead of supply. AMD is targeting over 50% CPU server share; 50%+ of a $200B+ TAM would imply a $100B+ server CPU business. Venice launch on 2nm benefits from more TSMC availability. Piper's Craig Johnson flags AMD as 'sweet spot to play Agentic AI.'

bullets.title: AAPL: Short at Hedgeye on weak iPhone 18 Pro lead times; Siri AI still lags frontier models
bullets.body: Hedgeye reiterates AAPL short: iPhone 18 Pro lead times are 0–11 days vs. ~25 days YoY, and the 2TB Pro Max model shows zero lead time despite a $200 premium. MS TMT notes the new Siri AI is 'substantially improved but still lags frontier models' with occasional hallucinations. TSMC shortages for 3nm/2nm and CoWoS remain driven partly by AAPL demand.

bullets.title: ORCL: Mizuho raises PT 45% to $351; investing in 1.7GW carbon-free Texas wind for AI data centers
bullets.body: Mizuho raises ORCL PT to $351 (a 45% increase) citing improved visibility and pricing power; Q1 FY27 strong with CapEx peak in FY27/FY28. Separately, Oracle announced investments in wind energy projects delivering 1.7+ GW of carbon-free electricity in Texas to support its Abilene AI facility, advancing toward 100% renewable matching for AI data centers.

bullets.title: INTC: Altera confidentially files S-1 for $2B+ IPO; potential optionality catalyst for Intel's 49% stake
bullets.body: Altera, which became fully standalone in Sep-2025 when Intel sold 51% to Silver Lake at an ~$8.75B valuation, has confidentially submitted a draft S-1 for an IPO that could raise over $2B and price as early as 2026. Intel retains a 49% stake. Barclays, Citi, JPM, and MS are underwriting. This represents meaningful optionality for INTC given the original $16.7B acquisition price in 2015.

bullets.title: CART: Down on DASH/COST partnership fears; Citi says relationship not exclusive
bullets.body: CART fell on reports of a potential DoorDash/Costco delivery partnership. Citi notes CART currently powers COST's white-label delivery but the arrangement is non-exclusive — Uber Eats is also a delivery channel for COST. Key watch is whether the CART logo is removed from COST's delivery page. Citi maintains its buy thesis on CART separately.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 1 favorites dominated, pressuring sportsbook holds; SCOTUS prediction-market case 70–80% odds states prevail
bullets.body: Hedgeye estimates gaming industry Week 1 NFL hold at 8–10% below average: favorites won 73% straight-up and the public ATS win rate jumped to 40% vs. 19% YoY. Separately, Citi notes legal expert Wallach puts 70–80% probability states prevail in the SCOTUS prediction-market case (oral arguments spring 2027), which would create a fragmented landscape but OSB operators like DKNG and FLUT could benefit via TAM expansion in white-space states.

bullets.title: RBLX/APP: MS OW targets $55 and $450; web distribution and mobile ad market key drivers
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reiterates OW on RBLX ($55 PT): web browser distribution and AI-driven creation reduce friction and improve discovery. APP ($450 PT) benefits from an $80B mobile ad market with ~1% conversion rates; improved targeting enables above-market growth for both APP and Vector.

bullets.title: CRM/ON Semi: Investor/Analyst Days on Sept 16; CRM last guided 26-Aug
bullets.body: Salesforce hosts its Investor Day at 16:00 ET on September 16; CRM last guided Q3 and FY earnings on August 26. ON Semiconductor holds its Analyst Day at 14:00 ET on September 16 — ON has historically provided financial targets at analyst meetings.

bullets.title: NYT: Guggenheim upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $82 on digital ad growth and margin expansion
bullets.body: Guggenheim upgrades NYT from Neutral to Buy and raises its price target to $82 from $70, moving its valuation framework to 2027. The firm expects low-double-digit digital advertising growth in coming quarters and 10%+ digital subscription net adds growth in 2027, with margins benefiting from normalization of operating expenses after 4Q25 investment spend.

bullets.title: SHOP/CLS/HUT: Canadian market weakness; SHOP -2.3%, CLS +2.0%, HUT -2.2% mid-morning
bullets.body: The S&P/TSX Composite fell 0.47% to 35,535 mid-morning. Shopify (SHOP) dropped 2.3% amid broad market weakness; Hut 8 (HUT) fell 2.2% in the crypto/digital assets sector. Celestica (CLS) bucked the trend, rising 2.0% on positive momentum.

bullets.title: DELL: Up 5.4% intraday, +350% over 52-week period; hitting new highs
bullets.body: DELL Technologies hit a new 52-week high, up 5.4% intraday and +350.4% over the trailing 52 weeks, leading 50 names making new highs in StreetAccount's daily screen.

bullets.title: VRT: Featured at Goldman's SuperCompute 2026 booth tour; CEO Albertazzi presenting Nov 17
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs is hosting SuperCompute 2026 booth tours in Chicago on November 17. Vertiv (VRT, rated Buy, $97.5B market cap) has an 8:30–9:45am CT session with CEO Giordano Albertazzi and product SMEs. NVT and ETN also featured.

bullets.title: UBER/TSLA/GOOGL/AMZN: Roth Capital launching robotaxi consumer adoption survey across 1,000 rideshare users
bullets.body: Roth Capital is fielding a proprietary 1,000-person survey of rideshare users in San Francisco, Phoenix, LA, Austin, Miami, and Las Vegas to assess robotaxi awareness, brand preference (Tesla, Waymo/Google, Amazon, Uber), price elasticity, and likelihood to use self-driving options if offered by Uber/Lyft.

bullets.title: ACN: Morgan Stanley hosting bull vs. bear debate Friday 9/18; AI displacement and bookings trends key
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley is hosting a virtual ACN bull vs. bear debate on Friday, September 18 at 1:00pm ET. Key topics include demand environment and bookings trends, AI displacement fears and IT budget crowding out, inorganic contribution and rising M&A valuations, and pricing environment read-throughs from global IT services peers.

bullets.title: ETSY: Oppenheimer upgrades to Outperform; +3.3% pre-market
bullets.body: Oppenheimer upgraded ETSY to Outperform in pre-market trading, sending the stock up 3.3%. No price target was specified in the available color.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Adopts Anthropic Claude for all engineers; Gemini Pro launch expected October
bullets.body: Citi TMT reports Google made Anthropic's Claude available to all engineers as a supplementary coding/research tool, signaling competitive concern about Claude's capabilities. Separately, GOOGL Polymarket odds reflect a Gemini Pro launch expected in October.
